result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Estimate current-flow betweenness from a random sample of node pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40685-L40789){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality( normalized=True, weighted=None, epsilon=0.5, kmax=10000, seed=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Approximate current-flow betweenness centrality](/assets/graphs/approximate-current-flow-betweenness-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by an estimate of current-flow betweenness from 96 random source-target pairs (epsilon=0.2, seed=1). The table sets each estimate beside the exact value: the bridge E comes out at 0.49 against 0.58 and the hub C at 0.46 against 0.43, close enough to rank the nodes, and the pendant G is exactly 0." width="100%"} `current_flow_betweenness_centrality()` sends current between every pair of nodes, which costs $O(V^2)$ pairs. This method (Brandes & Fleischer, 2005) sends current between randomly chosen pairs only and scales the result up, trading accuracy for speed: the number of pairs depends on `epsilon=`, not on the number of pairs in the graph. Use it for a quick ranking of a large network, and the exact method when the values themselves matter. Edge weights act as conductances. The graph must be undirected and connected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), estimate the normalized score; if `False`, the raw score, as in `current_flow_betweenness_centrality()`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights as conductances. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Weights must be positive. [epsilon]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Target absolute error of the normalized estimate (default `0.5`). The method uses `ceil((c / epsilon)^2 ln n)` random pairs, with `c = n / (n - 2)`, so halving `epsilon=` quadruples the work. [kmax]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of pairs to sample (default `10000`). If `epsilon=` asks for more, a `ValueError` is raised. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Seed for the random pairs, for reproducible estimates. If `None` (default), the pairs differ on every call. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to estimated scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, a weight is not positive, `epsilon=` is not positive, or the required number of pairs exceeds `kmax=`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each sampled pair costs $O(E)$ after one $O(V^3)$ inversion of the grounded Laplacian. The estimator is NetworkX's `approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality()`; the random pairs come from EdgeCase's own generator, so individual estimates differ. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 6 x 6 grid, a sampled estimate lands close to the exact values: ::: {#b669273b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec grid = ec.Graph().add_grid_2d(6, 6) exact = grid.current_flow_betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) approx = grid.approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality( epsilon=0.2, seed=1, return_dict=True ) round(max(abs(approx[n] - exact[n]) for n in exact), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.024 ``` ::: :::
